title: Turkey Meatballs with Zucchini Noodles
seoTitle: Turkey Meatballs with Zucchini Noodles | Firefighter Meal
subtitle: Classic flavors, lighter base
description: Classic flavors, lighter base. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.

steps.title: Form turkey meatballs
steps.instruction: Mix turkey, breadcrumbs, egg, parmesan, garlic, salt, and pepper. Roll into golf-ball-size meatballs.

steps.title: Bake meatballs
steps.instruction: Bake on sheet pans at 425°F 15–18 minutes until 165°F and lightly browned.

steps.title: Spiralize zucchini
steps.instruction: Spiralize zucchini into noodles; pat dry — wet zoodles steam instead of sear.

steps.title: Warm marinara
steps.instruction: Simmer marinara in a large skillet. Add baked meatballs to coat.

steps.title: Sauté zoodles quickly
steps.instruction: Sauté zoodles in olive oil 2–3 minutes just until bright green — do not boil dried pasta; these are zucchini noodles.

steps.title: Plate meatballs over zoodles
steps.instruction: Serve sauced meatballs over zoodles with basil. Lighter base, same hall portions.

proTips: Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
tonightSpread: Plate Turkey Meatballs with Zucchini Noodles with sides in separate pans so the crew can mix portions.
Portion bowls on the line with protein visible on top — crew eats with their eyes first.
Keep dressing and crunchy toppings in side bowls so greens stay crisp through second servings.
Line up Turkey Meatballs with Zucchini Noodles on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
Add a splash of stock or water when reheating — thick sauces tighten in the fridge.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Classic flavors, lighter base. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
substitutions: Any short pasta shape works — penne, rigatoni, or spaghetti.
